source: Dossier 11 §D7 and §D10.8 — the country table and its printed-alias layer.
note: The portal's own 251-row classifier did not transfer. Every Armenian name below is instead attested in the 71 accepted-shape declarations under evalkit/corpus, where it appears paired with its ISO-2 code. Nothing here is a translation written by hand.
null_name_note: A code with "name_hy": null is known for routing — border-office lookup, dispatch detection — and has no attested Armenian name. The code+name pair is then never written at all, which is dossier 03 §4.5's all-or-nothing rule doing its job: the portal keys these fields on the code and renders the name from it, so a name written without its code is dropped on import with no message.
alias_note: Aliases are printed forms as they appear on invoices and consignment notes, stored uppercase, matched on word boundaries, minimum three characters, longest match wins. ISO alpha-3 codes are deliberately absent: they are three-letter words that collide with ordinary text, and a wrong country code is legally consequential. A field whose whole content is an ISO-2 code resolves by exact match instead.
